From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** Buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller has tagged most clauses "[STANDARD]". Its note says these were "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we have "accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **We should not proceed on that basis.**

- The labels are the Seller's own description of its position. Nothing in the package shows the Buyer agreed to them.
- Every item tagged [STANDARD] matters to us, including the cap, thresholds, knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay.
- I have reviewed all 16 issues in full.
- **Action:** Before the mark-up goes out, confirm with the deal team that nothing has been agreed. The cover email should say expressly that the Buyer has not accepted any limitation or disclosure package.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A higher general cap, around 40–50% (AUD 9.6m–12m). This is justified by the identified risk profile: Bluefen alone is about 30% of revenue, and there is an open privacy incident.
  - Fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and fraud claims to sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50%, with authority to settle around 35–40%, and only if all carve-outs hold. (If W&I insurance is in play, recalibrate to the policy structure.)
- **Reason:** 20% is light for a target with known, unresolved, revenue-critical and regulatory exposures.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25k per claim. Basket of AUD 250k (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10k–15k.
  - Basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k), on a **tipping** basis (recovery from the first dollar).
  - Related or similar claims aggregated for de minimis purposes.
  - No thresholds for fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, covenant or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter on all of the above. Tipping and aggregation are the priorities.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket at 1% plus no aggregation lets the Seller avoid a series of mid-sized related losses (the Sandbar pattern is an example).

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims. Also, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties (at least two full audit cycles).
  - Tax: until 60 days after the relevant ATO amendment period ends (minimum 5 years).
  - Fundamental warranties: 6–7 years.
  - Specific indemnities: their own periods.
  - Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reject the default-application wording.
- **Reason:** 18 months may close before a second audit surfaces issues, and the blanket wording silently imports the short period into tax and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, shares and capital, solvency) capped at 100% of price.
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - 6–7 years (aligned with the NSW contract limitation period).
  - No disclosure or knowledge qualification.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. This is a non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** If title fails, we lose the whole asset; a AUD 4.8m cap on a AUD 24m share purchase is not acceptable.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 (limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) are drafted to apply to "all Claims of any nature," which would reach fraud claims.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out providing that no limitation, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance, knowledge or time-limit provision applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by:
  - the Seller,
  - its Related Bodies Corporate, or
  - its or the Company's officers, employees and advisers (pre-Completion).
  The carve-out should also preserve statutory misleading-conduct rights (ACL s 18 and Corporations Act s 1041H) to the extent they cannot be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Insist. This is a non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** A Buyer should never agree to cap or time-bar its recovery for being defrauded, and the Seller's "of any nature" drafting does exactly that.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:**
  - General disclosure of the entire data room "including DD-002 to DD-012."
  - Also the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records.
  - Item 1.4 non-admission.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Specific disclosure only. A matter is disclosed only if it is **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify its nature, scope and financial effect**, against a specific warranty.
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosure. At most, allow specifically identified documents to be referenced in a specific disclosure.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete the general disclosures. Item 1.4 is acceptable only if it is made clear it cannot expand what is disclosed.
- **Reason:** Blanket data-room disclosure moves all diligence risk to the Buyer and would neutralise warranties covering the very issues the Seller has identified.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is a broad anti-sandbagging clause that includes constructive knowledge.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Ideally, an express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not affect claims.
  - Fallback: excluded only where a matter was **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter. No constructive, imputed or adviser knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. If the Seller presses, use the fallback.
- **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, this would make every issue our diligence found (Bluefen, Ironquay, the incident, the bonuses) unclaimable.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:**
  - Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent.
  - Condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
  - The Disclosure Letter admits that no final consent has been given and that the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be met.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **Condition Precedent** requiring Bluefen's written consent under cl 11.2 that is unconditional, or subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably.
  - Evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The Seller to use all reasonable endeavours.
  - A Buyer-only right to waive the condition.
  - A long-stop date with a termination right.
  - A covenant that the Seller will not agree to changed contract terms without Buyer consent.
  - Fallback: a price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices within, say, 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Hard Condition Precedent.
- **Reason:** About AUD 3.6m (30%) of FY26 revenue depends on this consent, and the Seller's drafting would let a conditioned or incomplete consent satisfy the condition.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** Release of the roughly AUD 3.2m facility "following Completion." The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Repayment **at Completion**, deducted as Indebtedness from the price in the funds flow.
  - A signed payoff letter before Completion.
  - At Completion: a deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or discharges, and the return of title documents.
  - Confirm whether the security covers the Sale Shares.
  - Confirm that the change-control default in cl 8.1 cannot be triggered before discharge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release.
- **Reason:** The deal is debt-free; leaving the debt and security in place after Completion exposes the Buyer to acceleration under the change-control clause and to security over assets it has paid for.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not shown in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses treated as Transaction Costs/Indebtedness and deducted from the price, **grossed up** for:
    - employer superannuation guarantee (12%),
    - NSW payroll tax,
    - workers' compensation and other on-costs.
  - Payment through Company payroll at Completion, with PAYG withholding, funded by the Seller.
  - Any amounts payable after Completion (under the continued-employment conditions) also deducted or escrowed.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow and deduct them.
- **Reason:** These are legal obligations of the Company. If they are not deducted, the Buyer effectively pays about AUD 420k–500k more than the agreed price.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010) and is "considered adequate."
- **The real exposure:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 is not bank verification, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The risk is not the AUD 180k; it is that the Company may not own IP it relies on.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Payment confirmed by bank evidence and Ironquay's written acknowledgment.
  - An executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Condition Precedent or Completion deliverable.
  - A specific indemnity for **all** loss from any failure of ownership or right to use the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, licence fees, redevelopment and business interruption.
  - That indemnity to sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, and survive at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate and broaden the indemnity.
- **Reason:** The indemnity covers the invoice, not the IP title risk.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. The Disclosure Letter admits:
  - up to about 1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address,
  - access, scope and notifiability are unknown, and
  - no loss figure is stated.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the eligible-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act Part IIIC, and notify the OAIC and individuals if required, with the Buyer consulted and approving communications. The 30-day assessment expectation in s 26WH appears to have already run, given the incident pre-dates 22 September 2026.
  - A full incident report delivered before Completion.
  - A **specific indemnity**, outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure, covering:
    - regulatory penalties and investigations (the 2024 amendments increased the penalty exposure),
    - notification and remediation costs,
    - third-party and customer claims, including any Bluefen fallout.
  - Consider escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation and require a specific indemnity plus a covenant.
- **Reason:** This is an unquantified regulatory exposure that is known and possibly overdue for assessment, so it cannot sit within disclosed general warranties.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Full disclosure of the terms, authorisation and timing. Splitting into three may have avoided an approval or material-contract threshold.
  - The Buyer's election, before Completion, to have the Seller procure termination or non-renewal.
  - Any unpaid committed amounts treated as Indebtedness or a price adjustment if not ordinary course.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants requiring Buyer consent for contracts above, for example, AUD 50k, with related contracts aggregated.
  - These treated as a single "related" claim for threshold purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation; require clarification and a Buyer election right.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own letter says to read them together, which suggests a single AUD 330k commitment structured to look routine.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime: "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated," and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own regime:
  - General Warranty Claims
  - Fundamental Warranty Claims
  - Tax Warranty/Tax Indemnity Claims
  - Specific Indemnity Claims (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if applicable)
  - Covenant and Completion-obligation claims
  - Price-adjustment or leakage claims
  - Fraud

  Limitations should apply **only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended**.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default.
- **Reason:** The Seller's default quietly pulls every protection down to the general-warranty floor.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title to 100% is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. The letter itself notes this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Our own verification:
    - an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register,
    - review of the full issue and transfer history and the constitution,
    - confirmation of no options, convertibles, ESOP or pre-emptive rights,
    - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, including Riverlark security over the shares.
  - A full fundamental title warranty that is not qualified by disclosure.
  - At Completion: signed transfers, share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), board approval and register update, and releases of any encumbrances.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** The register is only prima facie evidence (Corporations Act s 1274B/s 176). Title is the core of the deal and needs independent verification and an uncapped-equivalent warranty.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, covering payroll tax and super on the bonuses, GST and income tax. It should sit outside the thresholds, carry a 100% cap and run for the ATO amendment period plus 60 days, with conduct-of-claims provisions.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, contractor and employee assignments, open-source use). Consider extended survival and a higher cap given the Ironquay issue.
  - Both to remain **open** items.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open; the Buyer has not agreed these.
- **Reason:** Both areas have live identified risks (bonus on-costs, Ironquay), so a 20%/18-month general regime is inappropriate.

---

## Priority summary for mark-up

| Priority | Items |
|---|---|
| **Non-negotiable** | 004 Fundamentals, 005 Fraud, 009 Riverlark at Completion, 014 Category separation, 015 Title |
| **High** | 006 Disclosure, 007 Knowledge, 008 Bluefen Condition Precedent, 010 Bonuses deduction, 011 Ironquay, 012 Privacy indemnity |
| **Negotiable (commercial)** | 001 Cap, 002 Thresholds, 003 Time limits, 013 Sandbar, 016 Tax/IP detail |

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Confirm with the deal team that no limitation or disclosure package has been agreed.
2. Request the Bluefen consent draft, the Riverlark payoff letter, Ironquay bank evidence, and the full DD-006 incident report.
3. Ask finance to rebuild the funds flow with the Riverlark repayment and the bonuses plus on-costs deducted.
4. Confirm whether W&I insurance is being pursued, since that affects the cap and threshold strategy.

The suggested percentages and amounts are negotiating positions for discussion, not settled market positions. They should be confirmed with supervising counsel.

- **Recommendation:** Delete. If the Seller presses, use the fallback.
- **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, this would make every issue our diligence found (Bluefen, Ironquay, the incident, the bonuses) unclaimable.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:**
  - Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent.
  - Condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
  - The Disclosure Letter admits that no final consent has been given and that the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be met.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **Condition Precedent** requiring Bluefen's written consent under cl 11.2 that is unconditional, or subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably.
  - Evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The Seller to use all reasonable endeavours.
  - A Buyer-only right to waive the condition.
  - A long-stop date with a termination right.
  - A covenant that the Seller will not agree to changed contract terms without Buyer consent.
  - Fallback: a price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices within, say, 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Hard Condition Precedent.
- **Reason:** About AUD 3.6m (30%) of FY26 revenue depends on this consent, and the Seller's drafting would let a conditioned or incomplete consent satisfy the condition.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** Release of the roughly AUD 3.2m facility "following Completion." The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Repayment **at Completion**, deducted as Indebtedness from the price in the funds flow.
  - A signed payoff letter before Completion.
  - At Completion: a deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or discharges, and the return of title documents.
  - Confirm whether the security covers the Sale Shares.
  - Confirm that the change-control default in cl 8.1 cannot be triggered before discharge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release.
- **Reason:** The deal is debt-free; leaving the debt and security in place after Completion exposes the Buyer to acceleration under the change-control clause and to security over assets it has paid for.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not shown in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses treated as Transaction Costs/Indebtedness and deducted from the price, **grossed up** for:
    - employer superannuation guarantee (12%),
    - NSW payroll tax,
    - workers' compensation and other on-costs.
  - Payment through Company payroll at Completion, with PAYG withholding, funded by the Seller.
  - Any amounts payable after Completion (under the continued-employment conditions) also deducted or escrowed.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow and deduct them.
- **Reason:** These are legal obligations of the Company. If they are not deducted, the Buyer effectively pays about AUD 420k–500k more than the agreed price.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010) and is "considered adequate."
- **The real exposure:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 is not bank verification, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The risk is not the AUD 180k; it is that the Company may not own IP it relies on.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Payment confirmed by bank evidence and Ironquay's written acknowledgment.
  - An executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Condition Precedent or Completion deliverable.
  - A specific indemnity for **all** loss from any failure of ownership or right to use the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, licence fees, redevelopment and business interruption.
  - That indemnity to sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, and survive at least 6 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate and broaden the indemnity.
- **Reason:** The indemnity covers the invoice, not the IP title risk.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. The Disclosure Letter admits:
  - up to about 1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address,
  - access, scope and notifiability are unknown, and
  - no loss figure is stated.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the eligible-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act Part IIIC, and notify the OAIC and individuals if required, with the Buyer consulted and approving communications. The 30-day assessment expectation in s 26WH appears to have already run, given the incident pre-dates 22 September 2026.
  - A full incident report delivered before Completion.
  - A **specific indemnity**, outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure, covering:
    - regulatory penalties and investigations (the 2024 amendments increased the penalty exposure),
    - notification and remediation costs,
    - third-party and customer claims, including any Bluefen fallout.
  - Consider escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation and require a specific indemnity plus a covenant.
- **Reason:** This is an unquantified regulatory exposure that is known and possibly overdue for assessment, so it cannot sit within disclosed general warranties.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three related renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Full disclosure of the terms, authorisation and timing. Splitting into three may have avoided an approval or material-contract threshold.
  - The Buyer's election, before Completion, to have the Seller procure termination or non-renewal.
  - Any unpaid committed amounts treated as Indebtedness or a price adjustment if not ordinary course.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants requiring Buyer consent for contracts above, for example, AUD 50k, with related contracts aggregated.
  - These treated as a single "related" claim for threshold purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation; require clarification and a Buyer election right.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own letter says to read them together, which suggests a single AUD 330k commitment structured to look routine.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime: "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated," and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own regime:
  - General Warranty Claims
  - Fundamental Warranty Claims
  - Tax Warranty/Tax Indemnity Claims
  - Specific Indemnity Claims (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if applicable)
  - Covenant and Completion-obligation claims
  - Price-adjustment or leakage claims
  - Fraud

  Limitations should apply **only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended**.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default.
- **Reason:** The Seller's default quietly pulls every protection down to the general-warranty floor.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title to 100% is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. The letter itself notes this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Our own verification:
    - an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register,
    - review of the full issue and transfer history and the constitution,
    - confirmation of no options, convertibles, ESOP or pre-emptive rights,
    - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, including Riverlark security over the shares.
  - A full fundamental title warranty that is not qualified by disclosure.
  - At Completion: signed transfers, share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), board approval and register update, and releases of any encumbrances.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone.
- **Reason:** The register is only prima facie evidence (Corporations Act s 1274B/s 176). Title is the core of the deal and needs independent verification and an uncapped-equivalent warranty.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, covering payroll tax and super on the bonuses, GST and income tax. It should sit outside the thresholds, carry a 100% cap and run for the ATO amendment period plus 60 days, with conduct-of-claims provisions.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, contractor and employee assignments, open-source use). Consider extended survival and a higher cap given the Ironquay issue.
  - Both to remain **open** items.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open; the Buyer has not agreed these.
- **Reason:** Both areas have live identified risks (bonus on-costs, Ironquay), so a 20%/18-month general regime is inappropriate.
